title: Separate a row schedule from structured plaintext before interpreting a confirmed lag
statement: Reproduced all 216 archived zero-offset selections and confirmation p-values. The extension uses four pinned sources, two independent row seeds per source, 104 synthetic ciphertexts and 10 nulls per ciphertext. Both offsets of the 40- and 50-token shuffle miss period 10 in all eight clean and eight 2%-erased cases, and reject exchangeability at lag 83 in all eight cases of an 83-letter repeated source passage encrypted with iid rows. Global shuffling confirms lag 10 for all eight 10-letter repeated sources under iid rows; eight, seven, six and six false confirmations remain for the width-16 and width-25 pairs of offsets respectively. With true source letters available, shuffling actual row indices gives no discovery or confirmation in any of 32 iid-row controls including both periodic sources. This conditional null recovers the planted period in all 48 clean and erased cyclic settings, and eight of eight drifting period-10 controls. It confirms the nominal 131 lag in three of eight phase-jump schedules. When six rows repeat in a least-period-24 cycle, it confirms five smaller lags (4, 6, 9, 11 and 12) and three correct lags. At the five false period choices, 6–7 of 24 row positions match on the reused schedule. This separates nonexchangeable row order from identification of its fundamental period. The conditional comparison requires the true input letters and known table.
check: Reproduce the previous and new counts from the declared sources, seeds, observed rates and paired nulls. For any proposed ciphertext-only lag method, compare schedules with the same least period but deliberately different reuse spectra, and train and test against periodic and changing source offsets before estimating a fundamental period. Benchmark candidate reconstruction against an independently specified known-column control, and report power on independent texts and epigraphic transcription noise with actual token collisions.

protocol:
# P-J-045, block offset and row-order calibration

Freeze the prior search: equality rate for ciphertext words at lag 2–160,
first 4,000 tokens discovery, 49 permutation maximum scores, shortest lag
with add-one p <= .05, next 4,000 tokens confirmation at that fixed lag using
49 independent permutations at p <= .05. Equal rates count against a claim.

Use the exact released Hermes Polygraphia III table (131 rows, 24 columns,
pinned SHA-256), normalized pinned sources filtered to its alphabet
and positions [4000:12000]. Four source pins, in order: Jan Hus Postilla
(Old Czech), Llull's Libre de Blanquerna (Old Catalan), Villon's collected
French verse, and the critical Galician-Portuguese Cantigas collection.
Pins can contain editorial text or many authors. Use two independent table
seeds 11321 and 11739 with 10000 times the index of the source added.
Independently seed plaintext structure, schedule perturbation, output noise
and stage nulls. Reuse each base text across settings.

One token represents one input letter and chosen table row. Build these
controls before any data-driven change:
- Historical text with iid row choices over 131 rows.
- Historical 10- or 83-letter excerpt taken from the same work and repeated
  to 8,000 letters, with iid row choices over 131 rows. Sample a distinct
  motif at a frozen random location in the 8,000-letter source window.
- Correlated, nonperiodic plaintext made by alternating between two
  disjoint source zones and drawing new segment locations and lengths
  of 64–160 within each zone, with iid rows.
- Distinct cyclic rows at periods 10, 24 and 131.
- Cyclic p=10 with 2% independent token erasure. Cyclic p=24 or 131 with 6%.
  An erased word is replaced by an identifier unique to its position;
  this removes equality and introduces no collisions.
- Nominal p=10 schedule with independent 1% phase holds and 1% double steps.
- Nominal p=131 schedule with occasional fixed phase jumps of +1, -3, +5
  at positions 1500, 4300, 6200 (zero based).
- Cyclic p=24 with 6 sampled unique rows reused four times each in a
  shuffled 24-slot cycle, and actual least cycle period reported.

Compare three null hypotheses. Global token permutation treats all positions
as exchangeable. Intact block permutations of width 16, 25, 40 or 50,
at offset zero or floor(width/2), keep fixed edge fragments and rearrange
the equal-width interior blocks independently in each half. The latter
conditions on within-block order. If width is a multiple of a period,
block permutations preserve that phase regardless of offset, so some
cipher schedules and source patterns share the same signal. Report each
width and offset separately; do not optimize the null based on the input.

The synthetic oracle tests exchangeability of table row order conditional on
the exact ordered source letters, the observed half's row multiset and fixed
erasure positions. Shuffle actual row indices within each half, re-encode
the untouched source, and reapply the original mask. This preserves repeated
source passages and individual row frequencies. It needs true plaintext and
the encoder, so no manuscript implementation is inferred.

Record selected lag, fixed-lag p, planted period classification and rate.
Separate empirical cases by distinct source pins and linked synthetic variants.
Use the same stage seed across null variants for reproducibility. No manuscript
text, period or key inferred.

validation.offset_phase_invariance: Verified for widths 40 and 50 and both offsets against period 10.

reproduction_python:
"""Calibrate the frozen equality-lag scan on known ciphertext controls."""
from collections import Counter
import csv
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import random

import numpy as np
from numpy.lib.stride_tricks import sliding_window_view
from vs import refcorpus

WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
TABLE_HASH = "fe3f24a46dbc6b655eab8dbbd75addf84ee4a7dbd387ad802af75d02edfe5b4d"
BOOKS = ("medieval_czech_01473c19", "old_catalan_54a4ab12", "fr_villon",
         "galician_portuguese_e5366bed")
SEEDS = (11321, 11739)
LAGS = np.arange(2, 161)
PERMUTATIONS = 49
CUTOFF = 0.05
HALF = 4000
SIZE = HALF * 2
BLOCKS = [(w, d) for w in (16, 25, 40, 50) for d in (0, w // 2)]
CASES = {
    "historical_iid": (0, 0, 0),
    "motif10_iid": (0, 0, 10),
    "passage83_iid": (0, 0, 83),
    "topic_iid": (0, 0, 0),
    "cycle10": (10, 0, 0),
    "cycle24": (24, 0, 0),
    "cycle131": (131, 0, 0),
    "cycle10_erase2": (10, 0.02, 0),
    "cycle24_erase6": (24, 0.06, 0),
    "cycle131_erase6": (131, 0.06, 0),
    "drift10": (10, 0, 0),
    "phasejump131": (131, 0, 0),
    "reuse24": (24, 0, 0),
}


def load_table():
    blob = (WORK / "hermes-polygraphia-iii.csv").read_bytes()
    assert hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest() == TABLE_HASH
    table = list(csv.DictReader(blob.decode("utf-8-sig").splitlines()))
    alphabet = list(table[0])
    codes = {}
    entries = [[codes.setdefault(row[c].strip(), len(codes)) for c in alphabet] for row in table]
    assert len(table) == 131 and len(alphabet) == 24
    return dict(zip(alphabet, range(len(alphabet)))), np.array(entries, dtype=np.int32), len(codes)


def recurrence(array):
    pad = np.pad(array, (0, LAGS[-1]), constant_values=-1)
    rotated = sliding_window_view(pad, LAGS[-1] + 1)[:, 2:]
    return np.count_nonzero(array[:, None] == rotated, axis=0) / (len(array) - LAGS)


def at_lag(array, lag):
    return float(np.mean(array[:-lag] == array[lag:]))


def smaller_period(cycle):
    return next(k for k in range(1, len(cycle) + 1)
                if len(cycle) % k == 0 and all(cycle[i] == cycle[i % k] for i in range(len(cycle))))


def topic_sequence(plain, rng):
    jumps, parts = [], []
    size = 0
    while size < SIZE:
        topic = len(parts) % 2
        width = min(rng.randint(64, 160), SIZE - size)
        start = rng.randint(topic * HALF, (topic + 1) * HALF - width)
        parts.append(plain[start:start + width])
        size += width
        jumps.append(width)
    return np.concatenate(parts), jumps


def make_input(plain, case, seed):
    period, erasure, motif_length = CASES[case]
    content_rng = random.Random(seed + 13)
    schedule = np.random.default_rng(seed + 27)
    row_rng = random.Random(seed + 51)
    input_info = {}
    if motif_length:
        start = content_rng.randrange(SIZE - motif_length)
        plain = np.resize(plain[start:start + motif_length], SIZE)
        input_info["source_motif_start"] = start
        input_info["source_motif_length"] = motif_length
    elif case == "topic_iid":
        plain, segments = topic_sequence(plain, content_rng)
        input_info["topic_segments"] = segments

    phase = np.arange(SIZE)
    if not period:
        rows = schedule.integers(0, 131, size=SIZE)
    else:
        row_table = row_rng.sample(range(131), 6 if case == "reuse24" else period)
        if case == "reuse24":
            row_table *= 4
            row_rng.shuffle(row_table)
        if case == "drift10":
            steps = schedule.choice((0, 1, 2), size=SIZE - 1, p=(0.01, 0.98, 0.01))
            phase = np.r_[0, steps.cumsum()]
            input_info["hold_steps"] = int(np.count_nonzero(steps == 0))
            input_info["double_steps"] = int(np.count_nonzero(steps == 2))
        elif case == "phasejump131":
            for index, jump in ((1500, 1), (4300, -3), (6200, 5)):
                phase[index:] += jump
        rows = np.array(row_table, dtype=np.int32)[phase % period]
        input_info.update({"unique_cycle_rows": len(set(row_table)),
                           "least_period_of_row_template": smaller_period(row_table),
                           "cycle_rows": row_table})
    mask = np.random.default_rng(seed + 81).random(SIZE) < erasure
    input_info["erasures"] = [int(mask[:HALF].sum()), int(mask[HALF:].sum())]
    return plain, rows, mask, input_info


def encode(plain, rows, mask, table, collision_limit):
    ciphertext = table[rows, plain]
    if mask.any():
        ciphertext[mask] = collision_limit + np.flatnonzero(mask)
    return ciphertext


def shuffle_block(array, rng, width, offset):
    copied = array.copy()
    end = offset + ((len(array) - offset) // width) * width
    blocks = array[offset:end].reshape(-1, width)
    copied[offset:end] = rng.permutation(blocks, axis=0).ravel()
    return copied


def null_sampler(mode, ciphertext, plain, rows, mask, table, codes):
    if mode == "global":
        return lambda rng: rng.permutation(ciphertext)
    if mode == "conditional_rows":
        return lambda rng: encode(plain, rng.permutation(rows), mask, table, codes)
    width, offset = mode
    return lambda rng: shuffle_block(ciphertext, rng, width, offset)


def compare(ciphertext, plain, rows, mask, table, codes, mode, seed, discovery):
    def null_for(start):
        stop = start + HALF
        return null_sampler(mode, ciphertext[start:stop], plain[start:stop],
                            rows[start:stop], mask[start:stop], table, codes)
    sample = null_for(0)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 100)
    max_scores = np.array([recurrence(sample(rng)).max() for _ in range(PERMUTATIONS)])
    p = (1 + np.count_nonzero(max_scores[:, None] >= discovery, axis=0)) / (1 + PERMUTATIONS)
    significant = np.flatnonzero(p <= CUTOFF)
    if not len(significant):
        return {"lag": None, "discovery_min_p": float(p.min())}
    selected = int(significant[0])
    lag = int(LAGS[selected])
    eval_score = at_lag(ciphertext[HALF:], lag)
    confirm = null_for(HALF)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 200)
    test = (1 + sum(at_lag(confirm(rng), lag) >= eval_score for _ in range(PERMUTATIONS))) / (1 + PERMUTATIONS)
    return {"lag": lag, "p_scan": float(p[selected]), "p_eval": test,
            "scan_rate": float(discovery[selected]), "eval_rate": eval_score}


def outcome(result, target):
    if result["lag"] is None:
        return "no_detection"
    if result["p_eval"] > CUTOFF:
        return "unconfirmed"
    if not target:
        return "confirmed_random_rows"
    return "confirmed_target" if result["lag"] == target else "confirmed_other"


def main():
    alphabet, table, codes = load_table()
    modes = ["global"] + BLOCKS + ["conditional_rows"]
    titles = [mode if isinstance(mode, str) else f"block{mode[0]}_offset{mode[1]}" for mode in modes]
    tallies = {case: {title: Counter() for title in titles} for case in CASES}
    records = []
    sources = {}
    for i, book in enumerate(BOOKS):
        pin = next(p for p in refcorpus.pins() if p["id"] == book)
        from vs import path
        assert hashlib.sha256(Path(path(pin["file"])).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == pin["sha256"]
        stream = [alphabet[c] for block in refcorpus.blocks_of(book) for c in block if c in alphabet]
        original = np.array(stream[4000:12000], dtype=np.int32)
        assert len(original) == SIZE, book
        sources[book] = {key: pin[key] for key in ("title", "period", "url", "sha256")}
        for seed in SEEDS:
            effective_seed = seed + 10000 * i
            for case, (period, _, _) in CASES.items():
                plain, rows, mask, info = make_input(original, case, effective_seed)
                encrypted = encode(plain, rows, mask, table, codes)
                rates = recurrence(encrypted[:HALF])
                search = {title: compare(encrypted, plain, rows, mask, table, codes, mode,
                                         effective_seed, rates)
                          for title, mode in zip(titles, modes)}
                target = info.get("least_period_of_row_template", period)
                for title, result in search.items():
                    result["outcome"] = outcome(result, target)
                    tallies[case][title][result["outcome"]] += 1
                records.append({"source": book, "seed": effective_seed, "case": case,
                                "nominal_period": period, "target_template_lag": target,
                                "parameters": info, "nulls": search})
            print(book, effective_seed, len(records), flush=True)
    payload = {"sources": sources, "records": records, "totals": tallies}
    (WORK / "lag-results.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
